key_insight: Unlearning updates made with standard full-parameter fine-tuning are often too small to survive aggressive 4-bit post-training quantization (PTQ); encoding unlearning as quantization-aware, low-rank adapter updates preserves removal of targeted knowledge after PTQ.
problem_solved: How to reliably remove targeted knowledge from a trained LLM while still applying aggressive low-bit post-training quantization for efficient deployment, without the model reverting to pre-unlearning behavior.
method: Encode unlearning as compact low-rank adapter updates (LoRA-style) that concentrate parameter changes in a small subspace.

Train adapters with quantization-aware objectives or simulated PTQ (e.g., simulate 4-bit rounding during adapter optimization) and apply reparameterization/scaling so updates remain representable after quantization.
Deploy adapter-only unlearning: keep the base model quantized (PTQ) and apply/fuse quantization-robust low-rank updates to maintain unlearning while preserving downstream performance.
impact: Enables practical, compliant LLM unlearning that survives aggressive 4-bit quantization—so practitioners can remove sensitive or proprietary knowledge without sacrificing model compression or inference efficiency.
